Scope: HEAD ad35fe0e (fix(rait-case): bind retries to case versions and audit the actual role). git diff HEAD shows no uncommitted changes under backend/ or apps/; the working-tree changes are round artifacts under work/rounds/R-0025 only. Review covered the two cycle-1 findings in delivery-review-A-C3-01-1.json, which is a recovered REVIEW result and not a bridge PASS.

Finding 1 (idempotency bound to version), resolved. In apps/rait/web/src/app/data/api/case.client.ts, triage/admissibility/admit/reject now derive the Idempotency-Key from {body, ifMatch}. The wire body, If-Match header, act and target arguments passed to postCommand are unchanged. A->B->A and re-save at a new ETag therefore produce distinct keys.

Finding 1, server side. In rait-case-command.service.ts, fingerprint() takes {actorId, ifMatch}, but only for triage, save-admissibility, admit and non-admission; every other command keeps the original command+target+payload fingerprint. The replay lookup still runs before the version check. An exact original retry (same key, same original If-Match) matches the fingerprint and replays the stored response once. The same key with a changed If-Match or a different actor fails the fingerprint check and returns 409 RAIT.IDEMPOTENCY_REPLAY, so a stale success is never replayed.

Finding 1, sensors. The e2e spec has: save all three, change one, then A->B->A, each expecting 200, a fresh ETag (5+3n) and the persisted assinatura verdict; same key with changed If-Match returns 409 while the original retry replays with the same ETag; same key/version from another authorized actor returns 409. The client wiring spec and triage page wiring spec cover key composition and re-save wiring.

Finding 2 (audit role attribution), resolved. The triage and admissibility controllers forward request.principal through @Req(), following the existing protocol pattern; the admit/reject controller signatures are unchanged. admissibilityAuditContext runs before the transaction, and therefore before replay or SQL. It fails 403 when the principal is missing, the actor id differs from the request context, or the tenant is not in principal.tenants. It then re-checks the existing isDetranActionAllowed helper for (inf:rait-case, triage) or (inf:rait-admissibility, create).

Finding 2, role selection. The audited role is chosen in this order: (1) the first DETRAN_POLICY_MATRIX tuple role present in canonicalRoles(principal.roles); (2) else an actual principal role that the helper authorizes on its own (covers existing wildcard/admin grants); (3) else permission-only, which records principal.roles[0] or null, with auditDetails {authorizationSource: permission, resource, action}. DDL 03-audit.sql declares actor_role as nullable text. The hard-coded triage and save-admissibility entries were removed from COMMAND_AUDIT_ROLES; admit, non-admission and the other commands keep their constants. The commit does not touch policy.ts, grants, PolicyGuard or the shared kernel.

Finding 2, sensors. The unit spec asserts 403 with no database call for missing, wrong-actor, wrong-tenant and no-grant principals. It confirms that secretary, existing ADMIN, permission-only with empty roles, and permission plus an unrelated role all reach the database boundary. The e2e test asserts audit.events actor_role equals the actual authenticated role for each role it tests.
